actual_scope: At p=19, beta0=-1/2, bandwidth 2, and t_i=i, is the 2-norm of the normalized Schur inverse strictly below 321 when bounded by the product of the certified 1-norm and infinity-norm?
scope_change_reason: The inverse 1-norm lies strictly between 281/100 and 282/100, and the infinity norm lies strictly between 18/5 and 361/100. The named next step is the square root of their product.
bottleneck_link: INVERSE-CONDITIONING.md bounds the 2-norm by the square root of the product of the 1-norm and the infinity norm. On this section that product of certified upper bounds is strictly below (319/100)^2.
stop_rule: Stop once the product comparison with 321 is complete. Do not compare the 2-norm with p^10.
evidence: research/gaussian-origin-inverse-two multiplies the residual upper bounds and also the round ceilings 282/100 and 361/100. The residual product is strictly below (319/100)^2. The ceiling product 101802/10000 lies strictly between 319^2 and 320^2.
